title: Product successor relation payload schema documents (13 relations)
description: The registered payload schema DOCUMENT for fact2 relation payloads, named by identity-and-evidence section 3 and native-evidence section 4.4. fact.payloadSchemaDigest is the raw SHA-256 of the EXACT FULL BYTES of this file; validation uses the selector the payload registry row names, exactly as the native and workflow import registries already work. This document has no root type on purpose: it is a multi-record bundle, and a bundle is admitted through its registry row, never by validating a payload against the whole document. ENCODING SUCCESSOR: fact2 payloads are canonical JSON C, not the inherited deterministic-CBOR profile. Every logical restriction that profile carried survives here as an admission rule - NFC text, no negative integers, closed field sets, enums, per-rung required/forbidden fields and the universe rule. Historical FactRecord1 CBOR bytes and their provenance are unchanged and remain valid history; they are never a fact2 preimage.

x-opensip-relation-registry.standing: Normative. Closed at 13 relations: the twelve inherited from fact-plane.v1 relationPayloadSchemaRegistryV1 plus native-evidence section 4.4 unresolved-edge.
x-opensip-relation-registry.payloadSchemaDigest: raw SHA-256 of the exact full bytes of that file
x-opensip-relation-registry.ladderAuthority: This registry is the SINGLE authority for every relation's resolution ladder, as identity-and-evidence section 3 states. `ladder` is that relation's total order over its OWN resolution methods, listed weakest-first, inherited verbatim from fact-plane.v1 relationRegistry.relations[].ladder (plus [observed] for unresolved-edge). Every other copy in the kit - native_evidence_model.v2.py LADDERS and capability-manifest-domains.v2.json RELATION-LADDER-DOMAIN-V2.ladders - is a declared MIRROR of this array and is drift-checked against it exactly and IN ORDER. A one-rung ladder is not a deficiency; it means the relation is fully determined at that rung.
x-opensip-relation-registry.rungsAreFieldRulesNotTheLadder: `rungs` is a different table: the per-rung required/forbidden PAYLOAD FIELD rules. It is legitimately the empty object for a relation with no per-rung field variance, which is every single-rung relation. Reading `rungs` as the ladder is the defect this key exists to prevent: an empty field-rule table must never be read as an absent ladder, and never as a licence to skip ladder membership. Membership is checked against `ladder`, always, with no fallback.
x-opensip-relation-registry.membershipRule: A resolution is admissible for a relation only if it is a member of THAT relation's `ladder`. A rung that is a member of another relation's ladder is refused, not accepted as a live vocabulary token; the flat rung vocabulary published elsewhere is necessary but never sufficient. Order comparison is the index within one relation's ladder; nothing orders a rung of one relation against a rung of another, and there is no global rank.
x-opensip-relation-registry.subjectKindLaw: What a subject-scope's `subjects` entries IDENTIFY, per relation. `source-path`: each subject is a path in the snapshot this scope names, so the scope's own extent is exactly those paths - `file` and `vcs-change` bind it through their registry snapshotJoins pathField, and `clones` binds it through bodyIdentityJoin, whose single anchor IS the body span the identity is over. `package-name`: a package identifier, not a path. `symbol`: an opaque SubjectIdV1 that the record associates with no path; the enumerator's attribution of symbols to files is trusted and is NOT re-derivable from the retained Run, so no per-subject path law is possible for these relations and any capability question about them can only be answered at the coarser retained extent. That limit is stated rather than worked around: inventing symbol-to-path parsing would be fabricated evidence.

anchorLaw.standing: Normative and CLOSED. Every relation row carries an `anchorLaw`; there is no default and no unstated relation. It decides how many `fact.anchors` entries a fact of that relation carries, and therefore whether one semantic input has one spelling or several.
anchorLaw.whyThisIsARegistryLaw: `fact.anchors` is `minItems`-free in the identity schema and only `clones` ever stated a cardinality. Every predicate written over the array - the `file` row's `anchorPathField`, and native-evidence section 1.2's `every one of its anchor paths` - is universally quantified, so at ZERO anchors it is vacuously TRUE and neither permits nor forbids that spelling. On the frozen v13 reference BOTH the whole-file-anchored and the unanchored spelling of one `file@enumerated` claim close a Run, with DIFFERENT fact2 identities (`5cce76d9...` and `d7bb2235...` over `tool/main.py`). A universally quantified predicate over an array of unstated length is not a closed law; the cardinality has to be stated.

source-text.rule: A code fact is READ FROM SOURCE TEXT, so it must name at least one anchor: the span it was read from. An unanchored code fact names no file that could have been read and is refused (`FACT_ANCHOR_CARDINALITY`). This was previously enforced only inside the syntax-universe capability guard, so the same unanchored `declares` or `references` fact closed a Run under a TypeScript or Rust universe; the law is one law and now binds in every universe.
source-text.noIdentityEqualityPromise: There is deliberately NO upper bound and NO canonical extent. Which spans a producer cites for a multi-span claim is a genuine semantic choice about what was read, so two conformant producers that cite different spans have produced DIFFERENT semantic descriptors and legitimately mint different fact2 identities. Nothing here promises cross-provider anchor identity for code facts, and asserting one would be a false equality between two different pieces of evidence.

body-identity.rule: Unchanged from the existing `bodyIdentityJoin.anchorCardinality`: exactly the body span the identity is over. Zero would leave the claim unattached and several would make the L0 recomputation a choice.

inventory.rule: An inventory fact is NOT read from a source span. Its whole semantic input is its payload, and that payload is already bound to the snapshot by this relation's own `snapshotJoins`: the path must be in the snapshot inventory, and for `file` the content digest, the byte length and CUSTODY of the exact retained bytes are joined as well. An anchor could only restate a subset of a claim that is already joined, and because nothing derives it, it is a free axis that gives one semantic input several spellings and several identities. It is therefore closed at zero (`FACT_ANCHOR_CARDINALITY`).
inventory.whatThisMakesRepresentable: Exactly zero is the only cardinality every inventoried path can satisfy, which is what makes the unconditional inventory promise honest: a path no bundled grammar reads (`tool/main.py`), an extensionless path (`LICENSE`), a data-document path, and - decisively - a `vcs-change` whose `changeKind` is `deleted`, whose path is by construction NOT in the analysed snapshot and can therefore carry no anchor at all. A cardinality of one would make that last case unrepresentable and would newly require the manifest bytes of every `package` fact to be retained, neither of which any contract asks for.
inventory.whatItAlsoCloses: The `file` row's `anchorPathField` was the only defence against an arbitrary anchor borrowed to satisfy an inventory claim, and it covered `file` alone: on frozen v13 a `package@manifest-declared` fact claiming `package.json` closed a Run while anchored into an unrelated `a.ts`. Closing the class at zero refuses that for all three inventory relations with one reason. `anchorPathField` is retained as the narrower per-row statement it always was; under this cardinality it can no longer be reached for `file`, and that is the point - the broader law subsumes it rather than leaving a predicate whose only remaining reading is the vacuous one.

anchorLaw.notAGrammarQuestion: Anchor cardinality and syntax-universe capability are different laws and neither substitutes for the other. The grammar-capability registry decides which relation@rung a SELECTED grammar can bear; this law decides how many spans a fact of that relation cites. Inventory capabilities are ungated by grammar at BOTH enforcement boundaries (see the native grammar-capability registry `enforcementBoundaries`), and independently carry no anchors at all.
anchorLaw.enforcedAt: identity-model relation_payload_rules, on every owning fact, at the producer boundary and again at retained Run closure. It is checked before the relation's snapshot joins, so the cardinality fault is reported as itself rather than as a downstream join failure.

coverageTotalityLaw.standing: Normative and CLOSED. A relation row carries a `coverageTotality` row only where the relation's own meaning makes its rung TOTAL over the snapshot inventory. A relation with no row declares that a subject may lawfully bear no fact, which is itself the record that nothing further constrains it.
coverageTotalityLaw.whyItIsNeeded: `entry.coverage: complete` is a claim that the committed examined partition was examined exhaustively. For a rung that is total over the inventory that claim also decides a universal negative: over a COMPLETE `file@enumerated` Coverage, `exists file where path=P` is authoritative, so a complete result that retains no fact for an inventoried subject asserts that an inventoried file is ABSENT. On frozen v13 that graph closed - a `file@enumerated` scope over the inventoried subject `a.ts`, `coverage: complete`, `deficiency: null` and zero facts. Nothing derived the obligation, so nothing refused it.
coverageTotalityLaw.whichRelationsHaveOne: `file@enumerated` only. A snapshot inventories exactly the files it contains, so every inventoried path has exactly one file fact and an omission is an error. `package@manifest-declared` and `vcs-change@vcs-reported` are NOT total and get no row: most paths declare no package and most paths were not changed, so their empty results are ordinary findings rather than omissions. Applying totality to them would manufacture obligations the relations do not carry.
coverageTotalityLaw.whatItDoesNotRequire: Only subjects that are IN the snapshot inventory are owed a fact. A scope naming a path the snapshot does not contain is answered honestly by a complete result with no fact for it - the host examined the question and the file is genuinely absent. And the law is conditional on `coverage: complete`: an `unknown` result with its disclosed deficiency owes nothing, which is what keeps a partially examined inventory representable.
coverageTotalityLaw.enforcedAt: identity-model close_run, over the RETAINED view's own facts and the retained snapshot inventory, alongside the other Coverage prerequisites. It reads no claimed value except the `complete` it is judging.

anchorLaw.rule: Every span this fact was read from; at least one, because an unanchored code fact names no file that could have been read.
Exactly the body span the identity is over. Stated here as well as in bodyIdentityJoin.anchorCardinality, which remains the enforcing join for the L0 recomputation.

bodyIdentityJoin.levelSpecificationRetained: normalisationVersion names the retained level specification bytes
bodyIdentityJoin.note: At L0 the canonical payload is the raw body-span bytes, so the host recomputes it from the enclosing fact anchor: a real source join. At L1-L3 it is a versioned normalizer output the host cannot recompute, so the requirement is exact retained preimage custody plus the framed-identity check. This is custody and framing evidence; it qualifies no normalizer.
bodyIdentityJoin.anchorRule: A clones fact carries exactly one anchor: the body span the identity is over. Zero anchors would leave the claim unattached and several would make the L0 recomputation a choice, which is the arbitrary-anchor defect in another form. `anchorCardinality` here is a declared MIRROR of this relation's registry `anchorLaw` (class `body-identity`, cardinality 1), which is the single enforcing statement and is applied to every relation before any payload join runs. The join checks that the two AGREE (`RELATION_ANCHOR_LAW_DRIFT`) rather than refusing the same fault a second time under a second name.
bodyIdentityJoin.languageIdSource: the BODY's language, from the SAME selector over the SAME single anchor that produces the body dialect: the `languageVersionBinding` of the fact sourceUniverse domain registry row, where `dialect.form` is `closed-suffix-table` gives `bodyLanguageByVariant[<the variant that table selects from this anchor's path suffix, longest match wins>]`, and any other dialect form gives `bodyLanguage`. The value is always a member of that row's `bodyLanguages` and of the closed foundation `#/$defs/body-language-version` `languageId` enum {javascript, rust, typescript}.
bodyIdentityJoin.languageIdIsNotTheProviderLanguage: It is emphatically NOT the domain row's own `language` field. That field names the ENGINE that read the body, and the two differ in both live cases: a `.js` body under `native.semantic-universe.typescript.v2` is a `javascript` body, not `typescript`, and every body under `native.semantic-universe.syntax.v2` would read as `syntax`, which the closed languageId enum does not contain, so a literal implementer would mint a different clone identity for every JavaScript body and NO admissible identity at all under the syntax universe. An earlier revision of this key said `the language of the fact sourceUniverse domain registry row`, which is that wrong reading; identity-and-evidence section 3 and each domain row's own `bodyLanguageLaw` always said the derived one, and the identity-model body-identity join has always checked the derived projection. This key is now the same sentence as those two.
bodyIdentityJoin.languageVersionSource: the raw 32 bytes of SHA-256(C(body-language-version)), the closed DERIVED record at foundation/identity-schemas.v2.json#/$defs/body-language-version, rebuilt by Run closure from the universe ResolvedInputs and the admitted retained native context the universe own nativeContextId names, per that universe domain languageVersionBinding. It carries the identity of the component that INTERPRETS the body span plus the selected source dialect; it never carries a human display string, an option-synthesis version, an operational platform value, a path, or a whole per-crate map. Fixed width, because the inherited frame gives each component a u8 length.
bodyIdentityJoin.tokenStreamFraming: u32be token_count || token*, token = u16be kind_id_len || kind_id || u32be value_len || value. The closure parses the retained L1-L3 stream to prove custody and framing; it does not and must not judge the tokenisation itself.

coverageTotality.matchLaw: A fact discharges THIS scope's obligation only if it agrees with the scope on EVERY coordinate listed in matchOn. Those are the four CoverageKeyV2 coordinates other than the subject-scope commitment itself, plus the owning snapshot. An earlier revision matched relation and resolution ALONE, and that is not enough in a view that carries more than one universe: the view-level fact/scope join is EXISTENTIAL - each fact must agree with SOME scope on relation, rung and both universes - so a TypeScript file fact is lawfully in a view that also carries a syntax-universe scope, and it then paid that scope's missing-file obligation. A complete Run exhibited exactly that (root diagnostic attempt3: two complete file@enumerated scopes for `a.ts`, only the TypeScript fact, ADMIT). Totality is a claim about what THIS universe examined, so it must be discharged by evidence produced in THIS universe; a fact from another universe is a different interpretation of the same bytes and is not the same observation.
coverageTotality.snapshotIsListedDeliberately: The owning snapshot is already forced transitively - Run closure requires every fact and every subject-scope to carry the Run's own snapshotId - so listing it changes no outcome today, and a control confirms the transitive refusal (REFERENCE_SOURCE_JOIN). It is listed anyway because this law reads ONE scope's obligation out of a SHARED view, and a join that silently depends on an invariant enforced somewhere else is the same class of implicit coupling that produced the cross-universe defect.
coverageTotality.rule: When a subject-scope for file@enumerated carries entry.coverage `complete`, every one of its subjects that appears in the analysed snapshot sourceInventory must have an admitted file@enumerated fact in the same view whose payload `path` is that subject. A subject outside the inventory is owed nothing.

snapshotJoins.note: anchorPathField closes the second-owner case: a file payload is admissible only under a fact whose every anchor lies in the very file the payload claims, so an arbitrary anchor can never be borrowed to satisfy a foreign file claim. It is universally quantified, so it says nothing at zero anchors and it never covered `package` or `vcs-change` at all; the registry `anchorLaw` now closes the inventory class at zero anchors and refuses the borrowed anchor for all three relations before this row is reached. This row is retained as the narrower statement it always was, not as the operative inventory defence.

x-opensip-relation-registry.snapshotJoinLaw: Normative. Each row states what the enclosing fact snapshot must contain for this relation payload to be admissible. Rows are applied by identity-model close_run on every owning fact; a relation absent from this table declares that it names no snapshot path and no retained artifact, which is itself the record that nothing constrains it.

CallsPayloadV1.description: Product successor of inherited opensip.relation.calls.v1 (fact-plane.v1 relationPayloadSchemaRegistryV1). Field set, types, enums, required and optional members are reproduced exactly; only the canonical ENCODING is superseded (C, not CBOR).

CanonicalPath.description: Inherited CanonicalPath: non-empty NFC project-relative path, slash separators, no empty/dot/dot-dot segment, no leading slash or backslash.

CanonicalText.description: Inherited CanonicalText: non-empty NFC text with no C0/C1 control characters. NFC text is an ADMISSION rule, not an encoder rule: C never normalizes. The host admits a relation payload only when every text value is already NFC, exactly as the inherited deterministic-CBOR profile required, and refuses otherwise.

x-opensip-digest.codec: SHA-256 over the fully framed domain-separated preimage: u8 len||domainTag, u8 len||levelId, u8 len||levelVersion (RAW 32 bytes, not hexadecimal display text), u8 len||languageId, u8 len||languageVersion, u32be len||payload. Unframed concatenation is FORBIDDEN.

payloadEncoding.L0-verbatim: u32be raw_byte_len || exact snapshot body-span bytes; tokenisation forbidden

x-opensip-digest.join: the frame is retained under the 64-hex suffix, so SHA-256(retained frame) equals it; the closure parses the frame and requires domainTag, levelId == normalisationLevel, levelVersion == the RAW 32 digest bytes of normalisationVersion, languageId from the fact sourceUniverse domain row, languageVersion == the RAW 32 digest bytes of the recomputed body-language-version projection, and at L0-verbatim the payload equals the enclosing fact anchor span bytes
x-opensip-digest.neverEquals: FACT-ID-V1. The fact identity wraps the complete clone fact and can never equal or substitute for bodyIdentity, by type or by domain (docs/coop/artifacts/fact-identity-policy.v2.json#/factRecordIdentityBoundaryV1/clonePayloadJoin).

x-opensip-digest.artifact: the exact retained canonical LEVEL SPECIFICATION bytes for this normalisation level: per-language lexical boundary rules, canonical token-kind registry, directive classification, transform order and replacement byte rules
x-opensip-digest.note: A human semantic-version label alone is insufficient, and this is never an opaque caller hash.

x-opensip-digest-law.standing: The closing digest law of identity-and-evidence section 3, extended to this bundle. Every DigestHex, Sha256Text and CanonicalPath field here carries x-opensip-digest naming its representation, producing preimage, codec, retention and owning authority. There is no default and no residue: a new such field added without an annotation is inadmissible. Coverage is asserted by consumed CHECKS in the Run closure, not by counting annotations.

retention.preimage: the exact preimage bytes are retained under this digest and the closure re-hashes them
retention.snapshot-inventoried: the value names a path in the analysed snapshot inventory, joined there
retention.provider-output-retained: the canonical payload is a versioned normalizer output the host cannot recompute; its exact framed preimage is retained so an independent replay can re-hash it
retention.not-joined: the value names a state outside the analysed snapshot and is deliberately joined to nothing; the reason is stated on the field and the closure records the exemption rather than leaving it as residue

x-opensip-digest-law.enforcement: identity-model close_run applies the per-relation snapshotJoins and bodyIdentity joins below to EVERY owning fact, after registered-selector validation and independently of the payload decode cache. A payload alone cannot decide snapshot truth, so the enclosing fact, the snapshot, the retained blobs and the bound native context are required owner context.
x-opensip-digest-law.residueRule: Consumed, not declared. Every x-opensip-digest field of a relation selector must be reachable from that relation registry entry snapshotJoins or bodyIdentityJoin, or must declare retention not-joined with its reason. An annotated field with no join, a join naming a field the selector does not have, and an unannotated digest/path field are each inadmissible.
